text:
ashok: FYI — incoming escalation from acme-corp. They report sharp p95/p99 regressions on tool/function-calling flows starting ~19:40 UTC after last runtime deploy.

ashok: Quick numbers from our observability: their /v1/chat/call-tool route p95 jumped from ~220ms -> 480ms, p99 from ~620ms -> 1.8s. Error rate is low but tail latency high.

ashok: Root cause hypothesis from initial triage: extra work in tool-router + synchronous JSON schema validation on the request/response path. We see a correlated CPU spike on the router hosts.

maria: Can you paste a sample trace or request id? I want to check spans.

ashok: Trace link sent to private thread (trace://runtimes/abc123) — key span breakdown:
```
span: request.receive 12ms
span: model.infer 160ms
span: tool-router.resolve 210ms
span: jsonschema.validate 350ms
span: response.serialize 8ms
```

ashok: So jsonschema.validate is taking ~350ms on the p99 sample, which aligns with the tail.

kevin: Ouch — that matches a pattern we saw in staging where we had Python-based jsonschema validation running synchronously on the hot path. For large tool responses validation can be expensive (deep nested objects).

kevin: Do we know if acme-corp enabled strict schema enforcement or full validation vs. fast/partial mode?

ashok: Customer config shows: "tool_schema_mode": "strict" (their app uses heavy nested arrays).

sara: Repro steps from support side (minimal):
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/call-tool -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"input": "run report", "tool": "generateReport", "schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"rows":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"string"},"payload":{"type":"object"}}}}}}'
2) Run with concurrency 40 and payloads that return 8-15 nested rows
3) Observe p99 on the router and jsonschema step

sara: I can repro locally with the above and see similar tails when schema has nested arrays.

olivia: Immediate mitigations for the customer:
- Flip their org-level flag to "tool_schema_mode": "fast" (skips deep recursion / full type coercion).
- Enable streaming response to reduce perceived tail while validation completes async.
- Route heavy tool calls to a separate pool with more CPU or async workers.

ryan: Customer is on Dedicated (reserved pool). They worry about correctness — they prefer strict validation but need reliable latency. Ask: can we offer a hybrid: synchronous lightweight checks + background strict validation that logs mismatches and optionally rejects on a later sync?

kevin: Long-term fix options:
- Move JSON schema validation off the critical path: accept response, stream to client, validate in background and raise a quality event if mismatch.
- Replace Python jsonschema with a compiled/wasm or Rust validator (we already have a PoC for a rust-jsonschema lib that is 4-6x faster on nested objects).
- Add per-org config to set a validation budget (max ms spent validating) and fallback behavior.

maria: Short-term patch we can deploy today: change router to do a quick shallow shape check in C++ layer (cheap) and only call full validator when shapes differ. That should cut the p99. I can prioritize a small change and hotfix.

ashok: Customer accepted temporary change to "fast" mode. I have their consent to toggle. Can someone run the admin API to flip it and monitor?

olivia: I can flip it. Command (admin-console):
```
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/admin/orgs/acme-corp/config -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"tool_schema_mode":"fast"}'
```
I'll run and then watch the org's p99 for 15m.

ops-bot: incident:update acme-corp-schema-latency mitigated: mode set to fast by olivia at 2026-03-15T20:12:03Z — monitoring for 30m.

olivia: Done. Initial metrics: p95 -> 240ms, p99 -> 420ms (so big improvement). Error rate unchanged. Customer notified and pleased.

ashok: Great. Next actionable items:
- kevin/maria: schedule Rust validator PoC evaluation and perf benchmarks (target 4x reduction on nested objects).
- maria: prepare short hotfix for shallow-shape-check (can be merged today, roll to prod tomorrow).
- eng-platform: add feature flagging API to allow per-route validation budgets and background-validate toggle.
- support: draft customer-facing note explaining safety tradeoffs and rollback steps.

kevin: Also instrument per-span p99 by org+route so we can alert earlier when validation dominates. Current alerts are per-cluster only.

sara: I'll capture repro artifacts and attach to the ticket (request ids + payloads).

ryan: I'll coordinate a post-mortem with acme-corp next week to discuss SLAs and staged rollout of stricter validation if necessary.

ashok: Thanks everyone. I'll mark this thread resolved once we see stable p99 for 2 hours and all follow-ups have owner.

maria: one more note — watch out for tool-router increased heap while validating large payloads; might need GC tuning on router workers if we run background validation.

ashok: noted. Closing loop later with metrics.
